output.proposal: HB No. 11217 seeks to create, under the Office of the President, the National Coordinating Council for Education (NCCE), a high-level inter-agency body chaired by the President, as the permanent mechanism for directing, coordinating and monitoring education and workforce development reforms across the Executive Branch. It aims to address the learning crisis and keep education reforms and priorities consistent across administrations.
output.alignment: As a government organization measure, the review should examine how the NCCE fits with existing education agencies and inter-agency bodies, including the mechanisms under Administrative Order No. 36, s. 2025 cited in Section 5 (Powers and Functions), and whether Section 9 (Rationalization and Convergence of Inter-Agency Bodies) adequately avoids duplication, consistent with the streamlining of the Executive branch and the reduction of overlapping functions under the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231). The review should also assess the creation of a new Secretariat headed by an Executive Director with the rank of Undersecretary under Section 8 (The Council Secretariat). The measure aligns with the Human Capital Development priority area of the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework, particularly its focus on equitable access to quality education. No LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda item is identified for this measure.
legislative_history: HB No. 11217 was filed on September 8, 2026 by Representative Antolin "Lenlen" A. Oreta III; it is pending at the filing stage, and later stages are not reflected in the available data.
HB No. 10697, filed in the same Congress, carries the same title and near-identical provisions.
HB No. 11275, HB No. 9573 and HB No. 10761, also filed in the 20th Congress, likewise propose a National Coordinating Council for Education but with different composition or design.

In the 18th Congress, HB No. 4925 and HB No. 2746 proposed a National Education Coordinating Council, and HB No. 7807 and HB No. 8022 proposed a National Education Council; only their titles were reviewed, and all are recorded as pending in the committee.
No substitute bill, committee report or counterpart measure in the Senate is identified.

output.salient_features:
HB No. 11217 seeks to establish the National Coordinating Council for Education (NCCE) under the Office of the President as the primary mechanism for coordinating education and workforce development reforms. Its salient features are as follows:
a. Section 3 (Creation of the National Coordinating Council for Education) provides that the Council is created under, and supervised by, the Office of the President, and shall align agency policies, plans, programs and budgets with the National Education and Workforce Development Plan.
b. Section 4 (Composition of the Council) provides that the President shall chair the Council and may designate a Cabinet Secretary as Vice Chairperson, with the heads of DepEd, CHED, TESDA, DOST, DOLE, DBM and DEPDev as members.
c. Section 5 (Powers and Functions) provides that the Council shall harmonize education policies and programs, implement and update the National Education and Workforce Development Plan, converge with existing inter-agency mechanisms, monitor priority reforms including those identified by EDCOM II, develop a human resource development plan for the education sector, and review and endorse major education sector budget proposals before their submission to DBM, among others.
d. Section 6 (Technical Working Groups) provides that the Council may create Technical Working Groups of senior officials of member agencies, of at least Assistant Secretary or Director IV level, and may invite other agencies and sectoral representatives.
e. Section 7 (Convergence and Accountability) provides that member agencies shall assist the Council, submit required data and reports, and be accountable for implementing aligned programs, under a results-based monitoring and evaluation framework.
f. Section 8 (The Council Secretariat) provides for a Secretariat as the Council's technical and program management arm, headed by an Executive Director with the rank of Undersecretary appointed by the President, staffed by permanent personnel and augmented by seconded personnel, technical experts and contracted specialists.
g. Section 9 (Rationalization and Convergence of Inter-Agency Bodies) provides that existing inter-agency bodies with substantially similar mandates or memberships shall, to the extent practicable, coordinate through the Council, whose meetings shall be deemed compliance with those bodies' meeting requirements.
h. Section 10 (Appropriations) provides that initial funding shall be charged against the current appropriations of the Office of the President, and continuing funding shall be included in the Office of the President's budget proposal in the annual General Appropriations Act.
output.related_measures_policy: HB No. 11217 may be considered alongside HB No. 10697, which is near-identical, and HB No. 11275, HB No. 9573 and HB No. 10761, which propose councils of the same name with differing compositions and mandates; consolidation of these measures may be considered. The measure aligns with the Human Capital Development priority under the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework. The review should assess the relationship of the Council with existing inter-agency bodies such as the Literacy Coordinating Council under RA No. 7165, as amended by RA No. 10122, and the mechanisms under Administrative Order No. 36, s. 2025, in light of Section 5 (Powers and Functions) and Section 9 (Rationalization and Convergence of Inter-Agency Bodies), and the need for a new Secretariat under Section 8 (The Council Secretariat), consistent with the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231).
